clue.text: Stylish performer in form on Court One

parts.note: a form is a school class
one as the article a

explanation.surface: A stylish tennis player shows good form on the main show court.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces are taken in answer order: A (one) comes before CT (court).
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: someone outstandingly polished and impressive at what they do is called this.

clue.text: Twin's shy with men

parts.note: to shy is to throw, cast
OR, other ranks, means enlisted men

explanation.surface: One of twins is bashful around men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shy' is the verb throw, not bashful.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: in myth, one of the Gemini, the heavenly brothers paired with Pollux.

clue.text: Third of Nottingham supports Forest with passion

indicators.note: in a down answer the letter stands under, supporting, the forest

parts.note: the Forest of Arden, setting of As You Like It

indicators.note: the third letter of Nottingham is taken

explanation.surface: A passionate fan of Nottingham Forest, the football club, backs the team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forest' is not the football club but the Forest of Arden; the definition is loose, an adjective for a phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: fervent, full of fire and zeal.

clue.text: Catch Penny breaking down — love is torture

indicators.note: the catch and penny break into the sad word, splitting it

parts.note: down means sad
a trap is a catch
O is love, nil in tennis

explanation.surface: A lover feels tortured when a girl named Penny breaks down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penny' looks like a name but is the coin abbreviation; 'down' means sad, not a direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an old form of torment where the victim is hoisted by a rope and dropped.

clue.text: Itchy? Tablets ordered that should prevent it

indicators.note: the letters of itchy tablets are ordered, put into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A patient with an itch is prescribed tablets meant to stop it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' is the crossword shorthand for sex, so the definition is a device to prevent it.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a medieval locking garment supposedly worn to stop sexual activity.

clue.text: Korean port a short distance ahead

parts.note: an inch is a tiny length
on as in moving onward, forward

explanation.surface: A traveller notes that a Korean harbour lies just a little way further on.
explanation.walkthrough: Inchon (now usually Incheon) is the port near Seoul, scene of the 1950 Korean War landing.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a harbour city on the west coast of South Korea, serving Seoul.

clue.text: Refusal reportedly straight from the horse's mouth?

indicators.note: reportedly means the word is as it is said, by ear

parts.note: nay is a refusal, an old word for no

explanation.surface: A rejection heard firsthand from the most reliable source.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Straight from the horse's mouth' usually means firsthand, but here it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Literal reading of an idiom: the sound a horse makes comes out of its mouth.

clue.text: Band not repeating support for hard working American

indicators.note: in a down answer the band sits beneath and supports the other letters

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
on means working, functioning

indicators.note: the band's doubled name is said only once, dropping the repeat

parts.note: Duran Duran, the 1980s pop group

explanation.surface: A band that never plays the same set twice backs a hard-working American singer.
explanation.walkthrough: Duran Duran is a British pop group; without its repeat it is DURAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: someone from Honduras is a Central American.

clue.text: Naked woman picked up in capital

indicators.note: picked up as in heard by the ear

parts.note: a nude Ellie, a woman unclothed

explanation.surface: A tabloid tale of a naked woman arrested in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, 'nude Ellie' gives the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the seat of India's government is that nation's capital.

clue.text: Not affected by team of stars

parts.note: a side is a team in sport
unaffected, genuine, real

explanation.surface: A team full of star players remains unmoved by its own celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: this astronomical adjective describes what relates to or is measured by the fixed constellations.

clue.text: Wanting a woman in work, though not much of a catch

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the letter of a is missing from the mix
the letters of woman in are set to work, reorganised into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone lacking a wife at work is said to be no great prospect romantically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wanting a' takes one A out of WOMAN IN, and 'work' rearranges what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny freshwater fish, so a feeble haul for an angler, and by extension an unimportant person.

clue.text: Scores showing great sharpness

definitions.meaning: perfect normal eyesight, measured on the Snellen chart

explanation.walkthrough: Read as figures, the answer is two scores side by side; it is also the measure of normal vision.
explanation.definitionFit: Eye-test term: normal visual acuity is expressed by this pair of numbers.

clue.text: Admit it's a bit limp — unworthy of review

indicators.note: review read as re-view, looking back, so the run is read from right to left
only a bit of the words limp unworthy is taken, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: A critic confesses that part of a limp production was unworthy of the notice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bit' takes PUNWO from inside limP UNWOrthy, and 'of review' reads it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Phrasal verb: to confess or acknowledge a fault openly.

clue.text: Accommodation in Euston? Who's travelling?

indicators.note: the letters of Euston and who travel about into a new order

explanation.surface: A hotel desk near Euston, a London rail terminus, asks which guests are travelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travelling' rearranges EUSTON and WHO; the 's of Who's is just 'is' linking to the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an urban dwelling, often a terraced home in a city, is a kind of lodging.

clue.text: Time to arrest every person racing cars here

parts.note: a day is a period of time
to nab is to arrest
each, as in each one

explanation.surface: Police set a date to arrest all the speeding drivers.
explanation.walkthrough: Daytona Beach in Florida is home to the famous Daytona 500 stock-car race.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Florida resort hosts a celebrated speedway, so motor racing happens there.

clue.text: Finances prevent Kelvin getting really good car

parts.note: to ban is to prevent
K is the symbol for kelvin, the unit of temperature
a Rolls-Royce, shortened to Rolls

explanation.surface: Someone stops Kelvin from buying a luxury car he wants financed.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to fund or back someone with money.

clue.text: Plot to replace queen in east, following orders

indicators.note: the plot takes the place of the queen's letter

parts.note: the Orient is the East
R is regina, queen
a bed is a garden plot

explanation.surface: A plot to replace a queen in an Eastern court, carried out under orders.
explanation.walkthrough: BED replaces R in ORIENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: compliant and dutiful, doing as instructed.

clue.text: Rubbish for a fighter

parts.note: scrap is rubbish, waste
per means for a, as in per day

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a boxer as rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a feisty brawler, someone who likes a fight.

clue.text: D's place out in the sticks

definitions.meaning: the letter D sits at the end of the word beyond
in a very remote rural area

explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, the phrase describes where the letter D sits in the word 'beyond'.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a remote, isolated place far from towns, the middle of nowhere.

clue.text: I get Nuala regularly playing cheeky parts

indicators.note: playing about with the letters rearranges them
regularly takes every other letter of Nuala

explanation.surface: Someone notices Nuala's cheeky behaviour while playing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes UL from Nuala; 'playing' rearranges I GET UL.
explanation.definitionFit: Anatomy: the buttock muscles, and cheeks are buttocks in slang.

clue.text: Gets relief from hearing joke

indicators.note: from hearing means the word is taken by ear

parts.note: wees, relieves oneself by urinating

explanation.surface: Someone finds relief from hearing a good joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets relief' means urinates, not finds comfort.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang: a clever trick or prank, a lark.

clue.text: Doctor hated smack — it's a killer

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters of hated are altered

parts.note: a smack is a blow

explanation.surface: A doctor who hated someone delivers a fatal smack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' rearranges HATED into DEATH; 'smack' looks like drug slang but means a hit.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a fatal stroke, the one that finishes off, is a killer blow.

clue.text: Drama over bagging royal bird

indicators.note: the drama bags, holds, the royal letters
over in a down clue means the drama is turned upwards, backwards

parts.note: Noh is classical Japanese drama
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A play about bagging a royal bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'royal bird' reads as one phrase, but royal is the wordplay and bird alone defines; Noh is a classical Japanese theatre form.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a long-legged wading bird of rivers and marshes.

clue.text: He runs a large pub

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
L is the size label for large
PH, public house, is the map abbreviation for a pub

explanation.surface: A man is described as the landlord of a big pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He' is the whole definition: any man's name fits it, and this one is built from the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a common male given name, so a he, a man.

clue.text: Sandwich maybe for selling abroad

definitions.meaning: Sandwich in Kent was once one of the Cinque Ports, a former port

explanation.walkthrough: Split as EX-PORT, the answer is a former harbour; Sandwich, a town in Kent, was one of the Cinque Ports, now silted up and inland.
explanation.definitionFit: Trade term: goods destined for foreign markets are described as being for sale overseas.

clue.text: Uncomfortably hot relative's about to strip

indicators.note: the relative goes about, around, the other letters

parts.note: an uncle is a relative

indicators.note: uncomfortably suggests the letters of hot are disturbed and rearranged

explanation.surface: A family member feeling the heat is about to take off some clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncomfortably' rearranges the three letters of hot into OTH, which 'about' surrounds; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to undress someone, removing their garments.

clue.text: Turning it round is laborious

indicators.note: turning means the word it is flipped to read backwards

parts.note: a ring is round in shape

explanation.surface: Someone complains that turning something round and round is hard work.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: exhausting, wearying work is laborious.

clue.text: Lower rent after Ray's moved

indicators.note: the hire part comes after the rearranged letters
the letters of Ray's are moved into a new order

parts.note: to rent is to hire

explanation.surface: A landlord lowers the rent once Ray has moved out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lower' is not 'reduce' but one that lows, i.e. moos: a breed of dairy cattle from Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a Scottish breed of cow, and cows low, so it is a lower.
